BREAKING: Driver Attempts to Run Over ICE Agents in Biddeford, Maine — Perfect Justice Delivered (Video)

July 13, 2026 Bruce Hoenshell
Listen to audio version of this article

Instaread

A driver in Biddeford, Maine, reportedly tried to run over ICE agents during an enforcement operation Monday morning and was shot dead by an agent acting in self-defense.

The incident happened around 7 a.m. near the intersection of Pool and Hill Streets. According to initial reports from authorities and witnesses, the driver accelerated toward an ICE agent. The agent fired in response, striking and killing the driver. No other injuries were reported, and there was no broader threat to the public.

Bullets in the windshield even though the libtards are posting videos claiming that the agents ran along side the car shooting through the side window!


Maine House Speaker Ryan Fecteau, who represents the area, confirmed early that a person was killed and ICE was involved. Biddeford police provided scene security but referred the full investigation to federal authorities, including the FBI and Maine State Police.

This comes just days after a similar case in Houston where a driver also reportedly rammed a law enforcement vehicle during an ICE-related stop. These incidents highlight the real dangers ICE agents face while carrying out lawful operations, especially when individuals choose to escalate with vehicles.

Advocacy groups have already begun organizing protests and demanding more details, but the core facts shared so far support the agent’s account of a direct vehicular threat. Officers are trained to respond to imminent deadly force — and a car being used as a weapon qualifies.

As the federal investigation continues, early reports paint a clear picture: the driver made a deadly choice, and the agent responded appropriately to protect himself and others on scene.

**Opinion Disclaimer:** This article is based on breaking reports, official statements, and witness accounts available at the time of publication. Full details will come from the ongoing investigation by federal authorities.
